Conversation, family & daily routines

keep a stiff upper lip phrase

also keep your chin up, chin up, be brave, bear up, take heart, stay strong

classical

Cic. Fam. 1.5.6: tū fac animō fortī magnōque sīs (Lewis & Short), s.v. spērō
Traupman 101, 102
Traupman 336

Fac ut animō fortī sīs!

fac with the subjunctive (ut may be left out); animō fortī, ablative of quality

be brave! keep your spirits up!

Cicero to a friend in trouble; the polite imperative fac (ut) with the subjunctive.

See also guts, encourage.

SourcesLewis & Short: fortis · Lewis & Short: animus

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 101, 336.

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
